To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
human disc large 1 (DLG1) is a protein that is altered by human HPV E6/E7 oncoproteins in organotypic keratinocyte cultures.
human papillomaviruses (HPVs) alter the tissue and subcellular localization and abundance of DLGI protein in organotypic rafts, and that this is observed for both high- and low-risk HPV types.
human papillomaviruses (HPVs) alter disc large (DL) expression in organotypic rafts of human keratinocyte cultures.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of DLG1 in the pathophysiology of HPV-associated neoplasia.
the role of HPV proteins in the expression and subcellular distribution of DLG1 in organotypic keratinocyte cultures.
the mechanisms by which HPV proteins contribute to the disruption of cell polarity in cervical neoplastic progression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DLG1 protein is altered in HPV-induced epithelial dysplasia.
the HPV E6/E7 oncoproteins are able to alter the DLG1 expression profile in organotypic keratinocyte cultures.

HPV E6/E7 oncoproteins are involved in DLG1 downregulation at the cell borders and in its accumulation in the cytoplasm, which may contribute to the loss of cell polarity observed in cervical neoplasia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HPV E6/E7 oncoproteins contribute to the changes of DLG1 expression and localization in the squamous stratified epithelium, which may have important implications for cervical carcinogenesis.

the HPV E6 and E7 proteins are able to induce changes in DLG protein expression and subcellular localization in organotypic keratinocyte cultures, and that these changes are similar to those observed in cervical lesions.
HPV proteins induce a loss of DLG-1 from the cell-to-cell contacts, which may have an impact on the control of cell growth.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HPV oncoproteins can alter the distribution of DLG1 in the epithelial cells and that this may contribute to the disruption of epithelial architecture and to cervical neoplasia.
HPV proteins can affect DLG1 expression and localization in the squamous cell differentiation pathway.
HPV proteins may contribute to the loss of DLGs in cervical lesions.
